rounds.text: UHM Vacation Ltd is trading at a heavily discounted valuation, highlighted by a trailing P/E of just 3.11x [E1] and a P/E of 12.47x against a sector benchmark of 25.59x [E5]. This mispricing is further underscored by a discounted cash flow model indicating an intrinsic value of Rs 385 per share, leaving a massive margin of safety of 92.4% [E31, E32]. Fundamental efficiency metrics are exceptional, featuring a robust 3-year median ROE of 38% [E15], a current ROE of 25.3% [E10], and a ROCE of 36.33% that vastly outperforms the sector benchmark of 7.56% [E8]. The business is also on an aggressive growth trajectory, with 3-year compounded sales growth of 33% [E11], 3-year compounded profit growth of 284% [E13], and an operating margin expansion of 15 percentage points to reach 16% [E17]. Financially, the company is almost debt free with borrowings slashed to just Rs 0.06 Cr [E26, E37] and a solid current ratio of 2.13x [E25], all backed by a supportive Consumer Services sector tailwind score of +0.88 [E45, E46]. Conceded: [E14, E20, E21, E22, E23, E39].

While headline profitability ratios appear high, a severe breakdown in cash generation presents a critical risk for UHM Vacation Ltd. Operating cash flow for March 2026 plunged into negative territory at Rs -1.67 Cr, driving free cash flow down to Rs -1.68 Cr [E21, E22]. This disconnect yields a deeply concerning cash conversion ratio of -0.27x against reported profit, with operating cash flow representing a negative 6% of operating profit [E20, E23]. Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has contracted by -13%, signaling a sharp deceleration from historical gains [E14]. Furthermore, the yearly operating-margin trend is classified as inconsistent over the last two years, while the company carries high debtors of 151 days, indicating significant friction in collecting actual cash from reported revenues [E18, E39]. Finally, the stock sits at the very bottom of its 52-week range, reflecting a complete lack of market confidence despite statistical cheapness [E4]. Conceded: the company maintains a clean balance sheet with virtually no debt, comfortable short-term liquidity, and high historical ROE and ROCE figures [E24, E25, E26, E38].

Conceded: operating cash flow for March 2026 was negative at Rs -1.67 Cr, resulting in free cash flow of Rs -1.68 Cr, a cash conversion ratio of -0.27x, and operating cash flow at -6% of operating profit [E20, E21, E22, E23]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months contracted by -13%, the yearly operating-margin trend is inconsistent over the last two years, debtors are high at 151 days, and the stock sits at 0% of its 52-week range [E4, E14, E18, E39]. However, this near-term cash friction and sentiment slump obscure an extraordinarily cheap valuation, featuring a trailing P/E of just 3.11x alongside sector-beating ROE of 21.39% and ROCE of 36.33% [E1, E7, E8]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt free with borrowings slashed to just Rs 0.06 Cr in March 2026, supported by a comfortable current ratio of 2.13x [E25, E26, E37]. The business operates in a Consumer Services sector experiencing a strong tailwind score of +0.88, while multi-year fundamentals remain robust with 3-year compounded sales growth at 33% and profit growth at 284% [E11, E13, E46]. Finally, a DCF valuation calculates an intrinsic value of Rs 385 per share against a market price of Rs 29.2, leaving a massive margin of safety of 92.4% that far outweighs short-term collection headwinds [E31, E32].

Conceded: the trailing P/E sits at 3.11x, ROE and ROCE outperform sector benchmarks, and borrowings have dropped to Rs 0.06 Cr [E1, E7, E8, E26]. However, the bull's reliance on these metrics ignores severe fundamental decay, most notably that compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has contracted by -13% and the yearly operating-margin trend is inconsistent over the last two years [E14, E18]. While the bull points to a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 385 and a 92.4% margin of safety, this model conflicts sharply with the market's verdict, which leaves the stock sitting at 0% of its 52-week range [E4, E31, E32]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes collection issues, but high debtors of 151 days directly fuel a collapsing cash profile where operating cash flow is deeply negative at Rs -1.67 Cr, resulting in a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -0.27x and negative free cash flow [E20, E21, E22, E39]. Finally, praising sector tailwinds does not erase the company's internal friction, as the dividend yield remains at 0.00% and institutional money flow sits strictly neutral, offering no safety net for shareholders [E3, E30, E46].
